subject.title: feat: AI safety event taxonomy — OTEL and Prometheus exporter mappings

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor these six AI-safety event types, metric names, and plugin SDK exports as a permanent core observability contract?
rationale: The branch creates a broad public taxonomy and security-sensitive plugin boundary; code review can identify defects, but it cannot decide whether this vocabulary and ownership model should become supported core API.

options.title: Sponsor and narrow the taxonomy
options.body: Approve the core direction, define the permanent minimum event and attribute contract, and require the exporter and producer blockers plus live proof before merge.

options.title: Keep safety telemetry plugin-owned
options.body: Decline the new core taxonomy and ask for an external diagnostics or safety plugin using existing generic seams, identifying any genuinely missing extension API separately.

options.title: Close the four-PR series
options.body: Do not adopt a first-class AI-safety observability product until a maintainer-backed design and concrete production consumers exist.

recommendation.title: Sponsor and narrow the taxonomy
recommendation.body: Approve the core direction, define the permanent minimum event and attribute contract, and require the exporter and producer blockers plus live proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a repository-wide core-versus-plugin product boundary and public-contract decision rather than a mechanical exporter repair.
